per_shot.note: Warm, lived-in hall; bunk lamp and arc lamp bloom and pool softly, star chart glows and reads; Gallery doorway is a dim slot with a tiny sign, so the wing does not announce itself.

Real museum mood: downlight cones, glass cases, placards, coloured pools on the floor; but halos are so large they swallow the stones (copper and gold read as glow blobs, ruby is a pink cloud) and the top third is dead dark.
Four tinted tanks light the floor and ceiling well, but the creatures read as pale glass statues rather than living light, the back wall is near-void, and the left tank is cropped.

top_issues.why: The showpiece is the cut stone; soft halos merge across cases so facets and shape are lost, especially copper, gold and ruby.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tighten the per-stone halo radius and keep a defined faceted silhouette inside each case; let the downlight cone and floor pool carry the spread.

top_issues.why: The brief asks for tanks glowing with living light; the creatures are flat translucent shapes that sit in the tank colour rather than emitting it.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each creature a brighter emissive core or rim along its body so it is the light source of its tank, and add slight value contrast between creature and tank fill.

top_issues.issue: Wing rooms are void above and behind
top_issues.why: Upper third and back walls fall to near-black; the hall has seams and fixtures, the wings read as a dark box with lit objects.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the tank and case light wash the back wall and ceiling ribs more strongly; a faint cool fill on the ceiling panels so structure reads while keeping dark corners.

top_issues.issue: Left vivarium tank cropped at frame edge
top_issues.why: The amber VEIL tank is cut in half, so the Long One reads as two hooks with no body.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Adjust tank spacing or the camera stop so all four tanks sit fully in frame when the suit stands at the centre.

top_issues.issue: Gallery entrance undersold from the hall
top_issues.why: A bought wing should invite the walk; the doorway is a dark column with a small sign.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Spill a hint of the gallery's coloured case light through the doorway onto the hall floor.

protect: Warm sanctuary light in the hall: lamp pools on wall and floor, glowing bunk lamp, readable star chart
Gallery staging: downlight cones, glass cases on plinths, placards, colour pools on the floor
Vivarium tank colours keyed to worlds (amber, ice-blue, sea-green, violet) and their light landing on floor and ceiling
Suit remains the clearest object in every frame

per_shot.note: Same hall with higher contrast and a glossy streaked floor; reads as more material but slightly less cozy, star chart darker and bunk lamp no longer blooms; Gallery doorway equally undersold.

Stones are crisper faceted gems with bright cores and tighter halos, so they read as specimens; long vertical floor reflections make a polished museum floor; cores near white bleach some hue (ruby, copper).
Creatures gain bright highlights and glints so they read more alive and pop from their tanks; floor gets coloured reflection streaks; void back wall and cropped left tank remain.

top_issues.why: Ruby, copper and the left-tank spider lose their colour in a white hotspot, weakening the per-stone and per-world hue reading.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap core brightness so each stone and creature stays saturated in its hue at the centre; keep white only for a small specular glint.

top_issues.issue: Wing rooms are void above and behind
top_issues.why: Upper third and back walls fall to near-black, so the wings read as lit objects in a dark box rather than rooms.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let case and tank light wash the back wall and ceiling ribs; a faint fill on ceiling panels so structure reads while keeping dark corners.

top_issues.issue: Floor reflections read as a wet mirror
top_issues.why: Long vertical streaks are effective in the gallery but make the hall feel cold and slick rather than a warm sanctuary, and the bunk-side warmth is reduced.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the glossy streaks in the wings but soften roughness in the hall toward A's soft pools; restore the bunk lamp's bloom and the star chart's brightness.

top_issues.issue: Left vivarium tank cropped at frame edge
top_issues.why: The amber VEIL tank is cut in half, so the Long One reads as two hooks with no body.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Adjust tank spacing or camera stop so all four tanks sit fully in frame from the centre.

top_issues.issue: Gallery entrance undersold from the hall
top_issues.why: The doorway is a dark column with a small sign; the wing does not invite the walk.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Spill a hint of the gallery's coloured case light through the doorway onto the hall floor.

protect: Crisp faceted stones inside glass cases with tighter halos
Creature highlights that make the vivarium feel alive
Gallery staging: downlight cones, plinths, placards, coloured floor reflections
World-keyed tank colours and their light landing on floor and ceiling
Suit remains the clearest object in every frame

why: B's crisper stones and glinting creatures make both wings read more as showpieces; A is warmer and cozier in the hall but its bloom swallows the specimens. The margin is small.
